source_name: CBCG – Centralni registar transakcionih računa pravnih lica i preduzetnika
why_relevant: Central register of legal-entity transaction accounts: maps which company banks with which bank. Reveals-indirectly the bank–corporate relationship graph and confirms a legal entity's existence/identifiers for entity resolution against tender award notices.

source_name: CBCG — Pristup informacijama (Free Access to Information)
why_relevant: CBCG's FOI (Zakon o slobodnom pristupu informacijama) entry point, including a public-registers/records subsection. This is the legal channel to request procurement plans, contracts and award decisions that CBCG does not proactively publish — important because no dedicated 'plan javnih nabavki' page was found on cbcg.me.

source_name: CBCG – Registar platnih institucija i njihovih agenata
why_relevant: Full list of licensed payment institutions and their agents — the non-bank acquirer/PSP layer that buys terminals, gateways and fiscalisation-compliant POS software. Names here become the seed set for company-level tender and contract-award searches.

source_name: CBCG – Registar banaka (Register of banks)
why_relevant: Authoritative enumeration of every licensed bank in Montenegro. Each bank is a buyer of POS/ATM/card-personalisation/software and most run their own tender or 'javni poziv' pages; this register defines the buyer population that other A2 cells must then mine individually.

source_name: CBCG – Registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata
why_relevant: E-money institution register: identifies fintech/EMI actors likely to procure card issuing, KYC, tokenisation and terminal services. Small population, high signal for a payments-vendor market map.

source_name: CBCG – Registar platnih sistema
why_relevant: Enumerates the licensed payment systems/operators in ME. Payment-system operators are direct buyers of switching, clearing and settlement infrastructure — a small but high-value tender-issuing population.

source_name: CBCG — Registar banaka (Central Bank of Montenegro bank register)
why_relevant: Authoritative local register that establishes, per bank, the exact legal name and the foreign parent group — the ground truth for building the parent-to-subsidiary map this cell depends on (entries observed for CKB 'member of OTP Group', NLB Banka AD Podgorica, ERSTE Bank AD Podgorica, and NLB Crna Gora DOO among receivables-purchase companies). Ownership changes here are the trigger to re-point group-level monitoring.

source_name: CBCG – Državne institucije / korisni linkovi (directory of Montenegrin state institutions)
why_relevant: Curated link directory of Montenegrin state institutions maintained by the central bank. Cheap, authoritative snowball asset for discovering further regulators, agencies and contracting authorities (and hence more tender pages) that generic search misses.

source_name: CBCG – Spisak platnih institucija i institucija za elektronski novac kojima je oduzeto odobrenje
why_relevant: Negative-list companion register (revoked authorisations). Prevents chasing dead actors and flags market exits — useful for dating changes in the buyer population between snapshots.

source_name: CBCG – Pretraga blokiranih pravnih lica i preduzetnika (blocked-accounts search)
why_relevant: Blocked-account / enforced-collection search. Financial-distress screen on bidders and awardees appearing in procurement records; also a due-diligence pointer when assessing local partners or competitors.

source_name: eFirma / CRPS portal (Uprava prihoda i carina)
why_relevant: The tax-administration-hosted face of CRPS, used for e-registration of companies and for accessing company records including beneficial ownership. Alternative access path if pretraga.crps.me is unstable; also documents the registration obligation for foreign software vendors selling into ME.

entity_name: Komisija za zaštitu prava u postupcima javnih nabavki
source_name: Komisija za zaštitu prava — Pravni okvir (laws and secondary regulation)
why_relevant: Authoritative pointer to the Zakon o javnim nabavkama and implementing rulebooks that define thresholds, publication duties and appeal deadlines — needed to interpret what must be published and therefore what is collectable.

source_name: LinkedIn company page — Procurement Services Ges.m.b.H, company of Erste Group Bank
why_relevant: Reveals the operating profile of Erste's central procurement entity: ~11-50 employees, HQ Vienna with own subsidiaries in CZ, HU, SK, RO and HR, three service lines (Sourcing for high-value strategic categories, Tactical Purchasing, Order Management), standardized supplier onboarding on a Supplier Code of Conduct, CIPS Ethics Mark. Category ownership and named sourcing managers are the practical route to identifying who decides Montenegrin payments spend.

source_name: ICT Cortex — Montenegrin ICT cluster (incl. Fintech Committee)
why_relevant: Cluster of ~40 Montenegrin tech firms with an explicit Fintech Committee working with CBCG on the National Fintech Strategy. Its member list names local payments-adjacent suppliers and partners (observed mentions: Financial Solutions, POS4.me, Payten, Euro-Unit Montenegro, Coinis, Logate, Amplitudo, Bild Studio). Primary snowball engine for the local supplier/partner side of the payments ecosystem.

source_name: ICT Cortex – Montenegrin IT cluster, member companies
why_relevant: IT cluster whose member list is the best single enumeration of Montenegrin software/integrator firms capable of bidding on banking IT tenders (Logate and peers). Doubles as a pointer to member news and hiring.

source_name: ICT Cortex (Montenegrin ICT cluster) — member directory by capability
why_relevant: Cluster directory enumerating Montenegrin ICT companies by capability category. Best single pointer for building the domestic supplier actor-map (who could bid on bank/public payment projects) before hunting their individual reference pages.

source_name: Asseco SEE (ASEE) — Group structure page
why_relevant: ASEE is the largest SEE banking/payments software vendor. The group-structure page lists local legal entities including E-Mon (Podgorica, Montenegro, 75%) — i.e. an identifiable local ASEE arm whose customers are Montenegrin banks/PSPs. Pointer for further entity- and customer-level searching (company registry, tender bidder lists).

source_name: Balkan Tender Watch (EU-funded regional CSO procurement-monitoring platform)
why_relevant: EU-supported Western Balkans coalition (Montenegro member: MANS; Institute Alternative also active) that has archived analyses, benchmarking tools and monitoring manuals per country since 2012. Its Montenegro document set is a pointer goldmine: it names the contracting authorities, watchdogs, datasets and systemic weaknesses (e.g. unreported post-award contract amendments) that shape how ME procurement data must be interpreted.

source_name: CRPS – Centralni registar privrednih subjekata (public search)
why_relevant: The master company register of Montenegro (legal form, status, founding date, legal representatives). This is the backbone for resolving bidder/awardee names found in tender notices into real legal entities, and for enumerating vendors by activity code.

source_name: Registar stvarnih vlasnika (Beneficial ownership register, within CRPS)
why_relevant: Beneficial-ownership register built into CRPS (operational since Aug 2021, 25% threshold, AML law basis). Exposes who actually controls local POS/IT integrators and bidders — essential for detecting that several 'independent' bidders share an owner, and for group-level competitor mapping.

source_name: DevelopmentAid — CBCG organisation profile (tender/award history for donor-funded work)
why_relevant: Aggregates donor- and IFI-funded tenders, awards and partner relationships for CBCG as an entity. Useful for reconstructing which international consultancies and vendors have already worked on CBCG payments and cash projects — a shortcut to the incumbent map.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore (Chamber of Economy) – member/association structures
why_relevant: Chamber of Economy organises members into sector boards (odbori/udruženja) including ICT. Membership and board listings surface the local integrator/vendor population that bids on bank and public POS tenders, and the chamber also republishes procurement and state-aid legislation.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore — Udruženje komunalne privrede (Chamber of Commerce, utilities association)
why_relevant: The association board membership is effectively a directory of Montenegro's municipal utility SOEs and their senior officers (e.g. Čistoća d.o.o. Podgorica is represented on the board). This is the cheapest route to a complete municipal-utility actor list for buyers that have weak or no web presence, and it snowballs into named contacts.

source_name: Udruženje banaka Crne Gore (UBCG) — Montenegrin Banking Association
why_relevant: All 11 member banks; runs a Payment Operations Committee and a Commission for Prevention of Payment Card Abuse, and comments on payments legislation. Industry-level coordination bodies are where shared infrastructure decisions (card scheme rules, interchange, fraud tooling, SEPA/instant migration) are pre-negotiated before any tender appears.

source_name: Banking Fraud Summit Montenegro (Podgorica) – agenda and sponsor list
why_relevant: Recurring Podgorica banking event (18th edition announced for 22 Oct 2026) whose sponsor and speaker lists identify fraud/AML/card-security vendors targeting Montenegrin banks — a niche the notice-bearing cells rarely capture early.

source_name: CEFTA Transparency Pack - Public Procurement country pages
why_relevant: Regional trade-facilitation portal that indexes each CEFTA party's procurement legal framework and publication portals in one place - a compact pointer for cross-checking Montenegro's stated rules against neighbours, and for discovering portals not linked from national sites.

source_name: KfW Development Bank — procurement guidelines and financed-project tenders
why_relevant: KfW finances Western Balkans financial-sector and SME-finance operations; procurement is run by the borrower under KfW's own Guidelines for Procurement, so notices scatter across borrower websites and aggregators rather than a single KfW board. Montenegro-located tender openings under KfW financing do occur (e.g. a WB6 Chamber Investment Forum tender opened in Podgorica). Track the guidelines to know where notices must land, and monitor borrower sites.

source_name: Montenegrin Foreign Investors Council (MFIC) – list of members
why_relevant: Enumerates foreign-owned companies active in Montenegro, including banks and payment/IT vendors (Payten confirmed as a member). Each member profile is a short company dossier — useful for building the vendor/actor map and for spotting new market entrants.

source_name: Open Contracting Partnership — OCDS Data Registry (search & bulk download)
why_relevant: Authoritative registry of which jurisdictions publish OCDS-structured procurement data, with API/bulk-download links. It is the fastest way to establish whether Montenegro (CeJN) has any machine-readable, standardised publication or whether ME data must be sourced from aggregators and scrapers instead.

source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore (Chamber of Economy) – ICT board and member directory
why_relevant: Statutory chamber with sectoral boards (odbor udruženja za IKT, odbor za bankarstvo i finansije) and a company directory; its board minutes and event announcements name vendor and bank participants. Classic pointer source for actor discovery in a small market.

entity_name: Vendor self-declaration cluster of Montenegrin fiscalisation software providers
source_name: Vendor self-declaration cluster of Montenegrin fiscalisation software providers (fiskalnakasa.me, v2-bit.me, tiramisuerp.com, e-invoices.online)
why_relevant: In the absence of an openly published approved-vendor register, the vendors who market fiscalisation/POS software in ME self-identify on their own sites. Snowballing these pages reconstructs a de-facto supply-chain map (who integrates with the tax authority, who resells terminals) and yields competitor names for A2 bidder analysis.

source_name: Ziraat Bank Uzbekistan — İhaleler ve duyurular (foreign-subsidiary tender page template)
why_relevant: Proof that Ziraat foreign subsidiaries do publish their own tender/announcement pages under a shared template. Strong hypothesis that ZIRAAT Bank Montenegro AD Podgorica operates an equivalent /ihaleler or /tenderi page; this page gives the URL pattern and Turkish heading vocabulary to probe for it.
